html:
SMTO-EXE-0250 — This Docker request was already sent once

GUID: ea8ef564-d559-5bfa-9a80-07ddc902117e
Slug: docker-operation-duplicate
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • The Gateway had already received this exact Docker request before, so it refused to run it a second time. The first attempt may already have made the change.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In this conversation, ask SMTO to show the current containers, images or Compose project status on that Gateway, without changing anything. This shows whether the first attempt already did what you wanted.
  2. If the change is there, you are done and don't need to do anything else. Running the same change twice could create duplicates or restart things unexpectedly.
  3. If the change is missing and you still want it, ask SMTO for it again as a new request, and approve it if SMTO asks. A new request is checked and approved on its own, so it can't be confused with the earlier one.

What success looks like

  • The Docker state shows your change once, either from the first attempt or from the new request.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't delete the Gateway's Docker record folder to force the old request to run again; it is what prevents changes from happening twice.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's persistent Docker execution record already holds this operation ID, so it refused to dispatch it again (including after a Gateway restart); the earlier dispatch may or may not have taken effect.

What this means

  • The persistent Gateway execution fence found this Docker identity already recorded and refused another dispatch, including after a service restart. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The persistent Gateway execution fence found this Docker identity already recorded and refused another dispatch, including after a service restart.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original durable receipt and exact Engine/registry state; changing the ID is not reconciliation.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the selected Engine and any registry read-only (docker.containers, docker.images, docker.compose_ps) to settle what the original operation did. If further work is still needed, issue a new, separately approved request, which gets a new operation ID. Do not delete the record under GATEWAY_DOCKER_STATE_ROOT (default ~/.smto/docker) to force a replay.
  • Inspect the selected Engine and registry state; do not replay an uncertain mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the selected Engine and registry state; do not replay an uncertain mutation.

How to verify the fix

  • The original operation is settled before distinct new work receives separate authorization.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
